mainTopic: Gift and inheritance wording for two people: רב ששת is proven right, and ריש לקיש is reconciled through תוך כדי דיבור
overview: Earlier, רב ששת asked about a man who gives one field to one person with gift wording and a second field to another person with inheritance wording. Does the second person acquire? רב ששת first brings a ברייתא about a father who left his sons a shekel a week and said that others will inherit the rest. He then pushes away his own proof: the 'others' may be people fit to inherit, following רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. רב אשי brings a stronger ברייתא, where property goes to one person and 'after you' passes to a second and then a third, and each one acquires in turn. That cannot follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, because under his view inheritance wording to an heir can never be cut off. So the גמרא concludes that everyone who disagreed with רב ששת is refuted. The גמרא then asks whether ריש לקיש is refuted too, but רבא ruled like ריש לקיש on this very issue. The answer is that the ברייתא is a case where both parts were said within תוך כדי דיבור, and ריש לקיש is talking about a case where the second part came later. The amud ends with the general rule that anything said within תוך כדי דיבור counts as one statement, except for עבודה זרה. The list of exceptions continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the shekel-a-week ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the father added that others will inherit in his sons' place, the sons get only a shekel, whatever wording he used.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...others will inherit in their place.' Whether he said 'give them' or said 'do not give them,' they are given only a shekel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that רב ששת is using as a proof. It sets up his point in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father says that others will inherit the rest, his wording no longer matters. The sons get only the shekel a week, because the rest of the property goes to the others. The 'others' were given the property with inheritance language, and that is the detail רב ששת will use.

keyTerms.meaning: others will inherit in their place
a coin; here, the weekly amount for the sons

phrases.english: others will inherit in their place,
whether he said 'give'
or whether he said 'do not give',
they give them only a shekel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא whose beginning is on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: Whether inheritance language works for a second person in a two-fields, two-people case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of a shekel a week for the sons, with others inheriting the rest

steps.title: This ברייתא is a two-fields, two-people case
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת points out that the ברייתא is like two fields and two people, and the 'others' still acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, it is like two fields and two people, and it teaches that they acquire!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת draws his proof. The sons got something like a gift and the others got inheritance language, and the others still acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shekel to the sons is like one 'field' given to one party. The rest, given to the others with inheritance language, is like a second field to a second party. Since the ברייתא says the others acquire, inheritance language seems to work in a two-fields, two-people case.

keyTerms.meaning: like two fields and two people

phrases.english: And here, isn't it so,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִשְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת וְכִשְׁנֵי בְנֵי אָדָם דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: that it is like two fields and two people,
and it teaches that they acquire!
phrases.notes: 'They' means the 'others' who were given the property with inheritance language.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּכִשְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת וְכִשְׁנֵי בְנֵי אָדָם דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: Inheritance language works for a second person in a two-fields, two-people case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The others in the ברייתא acquire even though only inheritance language was used for them

steps.title: רב ששת pushes away his own proof
steps.stepSummary: The 'others' are people fit to inherit, and the ברייתא follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He himself raised the point and he himself resolved it: it is talking about someone fit to inherit him, and it follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת rejects his own proof. The 'others' were relatives who could inherit anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that a person may leave his property with inheritance language to anyone fit to inherit him. If the 'others' were such relatives, they acquire because of their own standing. The gift to the sons does not help them, so the ברייתא proves nothing about two fields and two people.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: he raised the difficulty and he resolved it himself
someone fit to inherit from him

steps.confusionAlert: 'He' here is רב ששת himself. He is not arguing with someone else; he brought the proof and then took it apart.

phrases.english: He raised it
phrases.notes: He means רב ששת, the one who asked the question and brought the proof.

phrases.english: and he resolved it:
it is talking about someone fit to inherit him,
and it follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the shekel ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'others' may be potential heirs, who acquire with inheritance language on their own, following רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.title: רב אשי brings the ברייתא of a chain of inheritors
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes a ברייתא: 'my property to you, after you so-and-so, after him so-and-so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Come and hear: 'My property is to you, and after you so-and-so will inherit, and after the one after you so-and-so will inherit.' When the first dies, the second acquires. When the second dies, the third acquires. And if the second dies during the first one's lifetime, the property goes back to the first one's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a new proof by quoting a ברייתא. Here the גמרא only sets up the source; his explanation of how it proves the point comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first person gets the property with gift-type language ('to you'). The second and third get only inheritance language, yet each one acquires in turn. If the second dies first, the third gets nothing, because his right depended on the second; the property goes to the first one's heirs.

phrases.english: רב אשי said: Come and hear:
'My property is to you,
and after you, so-and-so will inherit,
and after the one after you, so-and-so will inherit':
when the first dies, the second acquires;
when the second dies, the third acquires.
And if the second died during the first one's lifetime,
the property goes back to the heirs of the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ששת's proof was rejected, רב אשי tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Inheritance language works for a second person when someone else received with gift language
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of a chain of inheritors after the first recipient (the inference is drawn in Step 5)

steps.title: The ברייתא is a case of two fields and two people, and the next recipient still acquires
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out that his ברייתא matches the 'two fields and two people' case, and it rules that the recipient acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, the case is like two fields and two people, and the ברייתא teaches that he acquires!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי now uses the ברייתא he quoted in Step 4. He says it is the same kind of case as 'two fields and two people,' and it rules that the next person acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, one person gets the property as a gift and the next person in line gets it in inheritance wording. That mix is what 'two fields and two people' means. Since the ברייתא says the later person acquires, this supports רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: Two fields and two people: a case where two different wordings (gift and inheritance) are used for two different recipients

phrases.english: And here,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִשְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת וּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: which is like two fields and two people,
and it teaches that he acquires!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּכִשְׁתֵּי שָׂדוֹת וּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא quoted in Step 4 to the 'two fields and two people' question.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that gift and inheritance wording for two people both take effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of 'my property to you, after you to so-and-so, after him to so-and-so'

steps.title: Blocking the escape that the case follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי heads off the earlier answer: if the ברייתא followed רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, the third person could not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: here too the case is about someone fit to inherit, and it follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. If so, how can the ברייתא say that when the second dies, the third acquires?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי expects someone to answer his proof the same way רב ששת pushed away his own proof in Step 3. He shows that this answer does not fit his ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 3, the proof was pushed off by saying the recipient was an heir and the ruling follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. רב אשי says that cannot work here, because his ברייתא lets the third person acquire. Under רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה that should be impossible, as the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces an expected objection
Fit to inherit from him, meaning a natural heir

phrases.english: And if you would say:
here too it is about one who is fit to inherit from him,
and it follows Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka;
if so,
[why does it say] when the second dies, the third acquires?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכָא נָמֵי בְּרָאוּי לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Protects the proof in Step 5 from the kind of rejection used in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that the ברייתא is about an heir and follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading cannot explain why the third recipient acquires after the second dies.

steps.title: Under רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, inheritance cannot be cut off
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב עויא taught that under רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, inheritance wording to an heir has no end, so the next person gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב אחא בריה דרב עויא send: according to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, if someone said 'my property to you, and after you to so-and-so,' and the first one was fit to inherit him, then the second gets nothing in place of the first. This is not gift language but inheritance language, and inheritance has no stopping point!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי backs up his question with a ruling sent by רב אחא בריה דרב עויא. It shows that under רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, the next person in line could never acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first recipient is an heir, the wording counts as inheritance. Inheritance passes on to his own heirs forever and cannot be stopped. So the 'after you' person never gets anything, and a ברייתא where the next person does acquire cannot follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent: a ruling sent as a message, often from ארץ ישראל
Inheritance has no end; once it passes by inheritance it keeps going to that person's heirs

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the earlier escape route fails here, and it sets up the final refutation.

phrases.aramaic: הָא שְׁלַח רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עַוְיָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Avya, send:
according to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
'My property is to you, and after you to so-and-so,'
and the first is fit to inherit from him,
the second gets nothing in place of the first,
because this is not the language of a gift
but the language of inheritance,
and inheritance has no stopping point!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא שְׁלַח רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עַוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the question in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא cannot follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling sent by רב אחא בריה דרב עויא: inheritance has no stopping point

steps.title: Everyone who argued with רב ששת is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that all the opinions against רב ששת are refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of all of them! It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: רב אשי's proof stands, and every opinion that disagreed with רב ששת is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא cannot be explained as following רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. So it shows that gift wording for one person and inheritance wording for another both take effect. That is רב ששת's position.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: an opinion is shown to be wrong from a tannaitic source

steps.whatToRemember: In 'two fields and two people,' gift wording for one person and inheritance wording for another both work, like רב ששת. The proof is the ברייתא where the next recipient acquires, which cannot follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, because under his view inheritance can never be cut off.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'תְּיוּבְתָּא' twice is not a repeat. The first is the claim, and the second is the גמרא confirming that the refutation stands.

phrases.english: A refutation of all of them!
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means everyone who disagreed with רב ששת.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument once the escape route is shut down.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The opinions against רב ששת are refuted. Two wordings for two people, gift and inheritance, both take effect.

steps.title: Does the same ברייתא also refute ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב אשי's ברייתא should also count as a refutation of ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this ברייתא is also a refutation of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the ברייתא which just knocked out the opinions against רב ששת should also knock out ריש לקיש. This is a suggestion that the next steps will test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that giving wording must be used for both recipients for the gift to work. The ברייתא uses gift wording only for the first person and just 'after you, so-and-so will inherit' for the next ones. Yet the second and third recipients still acquire, which looks like it contradicts ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say, a word that opens a suggested conclusion
A conclusive refutation of an opinion

phrases.english: Shall we say also
that it is a refutation of Reish Lakish?
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב אשי's ברייתא from the steps just before this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא נָמֵי תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the refutation from step 8 to a new target, ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that giving must be mentioned for both recipients
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the later recipients acquire even though only inheritance wording, not giving wording, was used for them.

steps.title: But רבא ruled like ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ריש לקיש cannot simply be refuted, because רבא ruled like him in three issues, this one included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? But רבא said: the הלכה follows ריש לקיש in these three issues!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the suggestion of step 9. It cannot be that ריש לקיש is refuted when רבא rules the הלכה like him in exactly this matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא ruled like ריש לקיש in three issues: קנין פירות, חליצה of a pregnant woman, and wording that mixes מתנה and ירושה. Since this case is one of the three, the ברייתא and ריש לקיש's view must somehow both be correct. That creates a difficulty that needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? A word expressing surprise at the suggestion

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not defending the ברייתא against ריש לקיש. It defends ריש לקיש, and it leaves the גמרא needing a way to reconcile the ברייתא with him.

phrases.english: And can you understand it that way?!
But didn't Rava say:
the halakha is in accordance with Reish Lakish
in these three issues!
phrases.notes: The three are buying land for its produce, חליצה of a pregnant woman, and mixing gift and inheritance wording, which is our case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא וְהָא אָמַר רָבָא הִלְכְתָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בְּהָנֵי תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 9 by citing a binding ruling, which creates a contradiction to resolve.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that ריש לקיש is refuted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's ruling puts the הלכה like ריש לקיש in this very issue, so he cannot be refuted.

steps.title: Within the time of speech versus after it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is a case where both parts were said within תוך כדי דיבור. ריש לקיש is speaking of a case where the second part came later.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here it was within the time of speaking, and there it was after the time of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by placing the ברייתא and ריש לקיש in two different cases. The difference is how quickly the second part of the statement was said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the inheritance part came within תוך כדי דיבור, the few seconds it takes to greet a teacher. So the whole thing counts as one statement covered by the gift wording. ריש לקיש requires giving wording for both people only when the second part came after that window.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; this opens an answer
Here... there; splits two sources into two different cases
Within the short time it takes to say a brief greeting

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
here it was within the time of speech,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ברייתא. The time of speech is about as long as saying 'שלום עליך רבי'.

phrases.english: there it was after the time of speech.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן בְּתוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִבּוּר כָּאן לְאַחַר כְּדֵי דִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two cases (אוקימתא by timing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא directly contradicts ריש לקיש, so he is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both stand: the ברייתא is a case within תוך כדי דיבור, and ריש לקיש is a case after it.

steps.title: The rule of תוך כדי דיבור, except for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that anything said within תוך כדי דיבור counts as one continuous statement, except in עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: anything within the time of speech is like continuous speech, except for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer of step 11 into a general הלכה. Words added or taken back within the time of speech count as part of the original statement, with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a rule that reaches far beyond inheritance: a quick follow-up or retraction is treated as part of the first statement. The exception is עבודה זרה. Someone who accepts an idol cannot undo it by taking it back within that short time. The sentence continues past this point with more exceptions.
steps.whatToRemember: תוך כדי דיבור כדיבור דמי: a statement added or taken back within a few seconds counts as part of the original statement. עבודה זרה is the exception.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule used across ש״ס for vows, gifts, קידושין and more. It explains how a quick correction can change the legal result.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
anything within the time of speech
is considered like continuous speech,
except for idol worship

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כׇּל תּוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִבּוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי לְבַר מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the distinction of step 11 into a binding general הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Speech within תוך כדי דיבור counts as one continuous statement in all areas except עבודה זרה (and other exceptions listed next).
